observations.observation: FERC’s September 29 order changed the schedule expected in PJM’s proposal: the filing was suspended for five months, effective February 28, 2027, so the proposed September 30 start could not proceed under that order. The order did not permanently reject the procurement.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The suspension was subject to further proceedings; the order also invited a new filing that could expedite a revised procurement.

observations.observation: Before the order, PJM had publicly targeted a September 30 start for a one-time procurement aimed at the 6,831 MW 2028/2029 capacity shortfall. The new fact was a regulatory suspension and further review, not evidence that the underlying capacity shortfall had been resolved.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The 6,831 MW figure is the stated regional procurement rationale, not a project-specific or Bloom-specific allocation.

observations.observation: The FERC order was qualified rather than a wholesale rejection: it found some parts of PJM’s proposal just and reasonable, identified three subjects for further procedures, and said a prompt new section 205 filing could potentially put the paper hearing in abeyance. The order also described bilateral matchmaking as an ongoing parallel process.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The order did not establish a replacement bid window or confirm that the revised process would occur on a particular schedule.
